moat_against: Per-project competitive bidding — no recurring revenue, backlog must be re-won
Cycle and customer concentration — growth is a leveraged bet on hyperscaler data-center capex
Scale disadvantage vs Quanta, MasTec and EMCOR on the largest campuses
Labor-constrained execution plus CEC/Stone Ridge acquisition integration risk
Building Solutions tied to soft Sun Belt housing
moat_for: Integrated site + shell model (CEC electrical) — site win gives pole position on higher-value phases and compresses customer schedules
Proven execution reputation with repeat mission-critical customers — 92% of E-Infrastructure backlog is mission-critical
Signed backlog $4.33B at 2026-06-30 (+116% YoY; combined $5.62B) — multi-year revenue visibility
Disciplined bid selection — exiting low-bid transportation work while margins expanded ~9pp in four years
moat_justification: Execution-and-integration edge in a per-project bid business: integrated site + shell/electrical model and schedule reliability expanded gross margin from 14.4% (FY2021) to 23.0% (FY2025) with ROIC proxy 31.8% in FY2025, but through-cycle ROIC was ~11-12% (FY2020-21), there is no recurring revenue or switching cost beyond a single project, and larger rivals (Quanta, MasTec, EMCOR) contest every award.
name: Sterling Infrastructure, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality cyclical contractor, moat 5/10 — record backlog and a real margin inflection, but at $424.36 it does not clear 15% (10.4% weighted, IV $250); it clears 15% only at or below ~$250.
